**Core assumption (falsifiable)**  
*“Solo or two‑person indie board‑game designers who are preparing a prototype will pay €39 per month for a print‑and‑play kit that supplies ready‑to‑print components, a rules‑sheet layout, and a play‑test feedback form.”*  

**Cheapest way to test it**  

| Step | What to do | Cost / Effort |
|------|------------|---------------|
| 1️⃣ Create a simple landing‑page | Show the kit’s value proposition, a mock‑up of the monthly subscription, and a **“Reserve your spot – €39/mo (or get a 7‑day free trial)”** button. | <$50 for a basic web‑host + free design tools (e.g., Carrd, Webflow free tier). |
| 2️⃣ Drive ultra‑targeted traffic | Run a 2‑day Facebook/Instagram ad campaign aimed at interests: *board‑game design, tabletop prototyping, Kickstarter board games*, limited to India/UK/US (where indie designers cluster). Budget ~ €30. | €30 ad spend + ~1 hour ad setup. |
| 3️⃣ Measure conversion | Count how many visitors click “Reserve” and actually enter payment details (or sign up for a trial). A conversion rate ≥ 2 % (or ≥ 5 sign‑ups from ~250‑300 clicks) would support the assumption; < 1 % would falsify it. | No extra cost beyond the ad spend; analytics built‑in to the landing page. |

**Why “now”?**  

- **Boom in indie tabletop games** – Kickstarter’s board‑game category has grown ~30 % YoY over the past 2 years, with > 4 k new projects launched in the last 12 months (source: Kickstarter stats, accessed Sep 2026).  
- **Improved home‑printing tech** – Affordable high‑quality home printers and printable cardstock are now widely available, lowering the barrier to produce professional‑looking components.  
- **Fragmented play‑testing workflow** – Designers still cobble together PDFs, print them, and manually collect notes; no dedicated SaaS solution exists for this niche.  

These trends create a narrow window where a low‑cost, subscription‑based print‑and‑play kit can meet a real, growing demand.

```
“Solo or two‑person indie board‑game designers preparing a prototype will pay €39 per month for a print‑and‑play kit that supplies ready‑to‑print components, a rules‑sheet layout, and a play‑test feedback form.”

Cheapest way to test it:
1. Build a one‑page landing site with a €39/mo sign‑up button (or free trial).
2. Run a €30, 2‑day targeted ad to board‑game‑design audiences.
3. Track sign‑up conversion; ≥2 % conversion → assumption holds, <1 % → falsified.
```

## Idea

Kindling is a print-and-play kit for indie board-game designers: card, board and token templates that print true on a home printer, a rules-sheet layout, and a playtest feedback form that sorts what testers say. €39 a month.

Solo and two-person indie board-game designers preparing a prototype for playtests, conventions or a Kickstarter. They lose evenings fighting print margins and collecting scattered playtest notes.
